intro.data: An adjunction comes with two special arrows. The UNIT η starts a round trip — it wraps a value up. The COUNIT ε ends one — it evaluates back down. For currying, the unit pairs a value with an argument, and the counit is exactly function APPLICATION: (g, a) ↦ g(a). Match each piece of the adjunction to what it is. Watch out: an adjunction is NOT an inverse — that's the impostor.
intro.alchemy: An adjunction comes with two special steps. The UNIT η starts a round trip (compound up); the COUNIT ε ends one (distil back). Match each piece to what it is — and avoid the impostor that calls it an inverse.
intro.spellcraft: An adjunction comes with two special workings. The UNIT η starts a round trip (bind up); the COUNIT ε ends one (release back). Match each piece to what it is — and avoid the impostor that calls it an inverse.
intro.abstract: An adjunction F ⊣ G has a unit η : 1 ⇒ GF and counit ε : FG ⇒ 1 (here for currying). Match each named piece to its description. A distractor mis-describes the adjunction as an inverse.

afterSuccess.data: You matched the three pieces: the bijection (the perfect one-to-one pairing), the unit η (pairing — start the round trip), and the counit ε (evaluation — end it). For currying, the counit is exactly function application, (g, a) ↦ g(a) — that everyday 'apply' is a counit! And the impostor was the trap: an adjunction is NOT an inverse; F and G needn't undo each other, only correspond. Unit and counit, tied by the triangle identities, are the whole story.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You matched the bijection, the unit (compound — start), and the counit (distil — end). The impostor was the trap: an adjunction is not an inverse. Unit and counit, tied by the triangle identities, are the whole story.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You matched the bijection, the unit (bind — start), and the counit (release — end). The impostor was the trap: an adjunction is not an inverse. Unit and counit, tied by the triangle identities, are the whole story.
afterSuccess.abstract: η : 1 ⇒ GF and ε : FG ⇒ 1 present the adjunction without mentioning hom-sets; the triangle identities (εF)∘(Fη)=id, (Gε)∘(ηG)=id make them coherent. An adjunction is weaker than an equivalence — F and G need not be inverse.

reveal.summary: Every adjunction F ⊣ G has a unit η : A → G(F(A)) (start the round trip) and a counit ε : F(G(B)) → B (end it), tied by the triangle identities. For currying, the counit is function application. An adjunction is a correspondence, not an inverse.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: The counit of currying is eval: (f, x) => f(x). The unit pairs: c => a => [c, a].
